previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for nausea, vomiting, and periumbilical abdominal pain. She has a history of insulin-dependent diabetes, stage 5 chronic kidney disease on peritoneal dialysis, gastroparesis, and chronic constipation. She recently had bloody drainage from her PD catheter site and was started on Bactrim. During this admission, she developed worsening nausea and abdominal discomfort. CT imaging showed no intra-abdominal pathology, and peritoneal fluid analysis did not indicate peritonitis. She was found to have a superficial soft tissue infection at the catheter site with erythema and yellow drainage. Her symptoms improved with supportive care, and she transitioned to clindamycin and gentamicin cream for the infection. She tolerated oral intake by discharge and was sent home with instructions to continue her bowel regimen, complete the antibiotic course, monitor the catheter site, and follow up for a pelvic ultrasound in one year to evaluate a right adnexal cyst.
